claude.performance_metric: Blue Ribbon Chapter 11 (Jan 2020) then brands fully divested by Sept 2021; Ceridian sold down to ~5.3%; FY2021 net loss $(287.0)M
claude.rationale: This slice is a holding-company split-off in which the contributed businesses were separately disclosed and progressively divested (Ceridian sold down to ~5.3%; Blue Ribbon entered Chapter 11 and its brands were fully divested by September 2021), and the documented adverse driver of operating decline is exogenous (COVID-19 guest-count reduction and dining-room closures from late March 2020), not a documented product/process alignment failure or operations/organization fracture. No slice line documents disruption specifically at the product/process interface (p4) or an operations-vs-people/management/culture fracture (p5); the discontinuities described are portfolio divestitures and a pandemic shock rather than realized integration-interface breakdowns. Because the slice concerns a diversified holding-company vehicle rather than an integrating merger, it does not permit determination of these interface pathways, so p4 and p5 are coded uncertain.

gemini.rationale: The slice documents the progressive divestiture of Ceridian and the bankruptcy/reorganization of American Blue Ribbon Holdings, as well as COVID-19 impacts on the Restaurant Group. There is no documented evidence of product/process incoherence (p4) or process/organization fracture (p5) driving these outcomes.

openai.performance_metric: Ceridian stake reduced to approximately 5.3% by the FY2021 filing date
openai.rationale: The slice documents divestitures, Blue Ribbon's Chapter 11 reorganization, and COVID-19-driven restaurant disruption, but it does not attribute these outcomes to an acquired-product/operating-process misalignment; therefore p4 is 0. It likewise provides no evidence that operational integration fractured against management, employees, or culture over time, so p5 is 0.
